fields.title: Air quality observations and forecast, Sawmill County: Coyote Draw Fire smoke
fields.note: Observed values are hourly NowCast PM2.5 AQI on the May 2024 breakpoints. NowCast trails fast-changing smoke, so near-ground levels in Pine Gulch may already be higher than shown. The Kestrel Springs sensor is a temporary unit with lower accuracy than a regulatory monitor. Forecasts assume west-northwest winds keep pushing the Coyote Draw Fire plume east-southeast through the evening; a wind shift or more fire growth will change them. CDPHE is drafting a smoke advisory for Sawmill County. Until it is issued, everyone in Pine Gulch and Kestrel Springs should limit time outdoors. People with heart or lung disease, older adults and children should stay indoors with filtered air.

instructorNote: Display the board, then read the superintendent's call (31 students in an unventilated gym), the medical center house supervisor's call (3 COPD inpatients, transfers to Denver?) and the Red Cross note (high school shelter opens 16:15, animal team at the fairgrounds) from the MSEL. Watch for: the EM starting the EOP 7 actions for AQI 151 or higher (Recreation Center clean air shelter) and confirming the shelters on the board; the Fire Chief giving the hospital the PG-03 arrival times; and the 31 students going by bus to the high school for reunification instead of being released into the smoke.
